Dolynske Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dolynske, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery existed by 1910, though only its postwar section retains legible dated tombstones today. Jewish settlement in Dolynske (known as Valegotsulovo until 1945) dates to the early 19th century; a pogrom struck the community on March 21, 1882. Population reached 1,865 (20%) by 1897 and 2,650 (15%) by 1910, when three synagogues and two Jewish cemeteries operated, before declining to 1,105 by 1923 and 541 by 1939. About 300 Jews were executed by Germans on August 29, 1941. Notable native son Lazare Saminsky, the Jewish composer, was born in Dolynske.
